title: A person's deliberate block on u9h was silently dropped by the run's own merge, which then dispatched the attempt the block existed to stop
body: At 18:41:09 local the session lead committed 1b725f49 (origin/main): tick 37i created and "37i" added to u9h's blocked_by, so the run 'stops cycling on it and stops spending interventions'. At 18:43:32 the run's merge 96977e99 (origin/main into epic/dha) resolved .tick/issues/u9h.json byte-identical to the run side (git diff 3c706e57 96977e99 -- .tick/issues/u9h.json is empty), deleting the "37i" entry; the claim (f97f8cb3) and the graph read that admitted u9h both happened before the merge, so the block was never visible to the orchestrator, which dispatched attempt 22 two minutes after the block was committed — spending the go6 intervention the block existed to prevent. The shape: a file the run rewrites (.tick/issues/<tick>.json) receives a human edit on main, and the run's merge resolution takes its own side verbatim, so any person's governance edit to a live tick is silently reverted while a run is mid-claim; the reconciler's tick-graph read must happen after the main merge and before dispatch, and a merge that drops a blocked_by entry added by a non-run author must fail loudly rather than resolve.
